products.observed: A clean v3 laboratory run attempted all four locally eligible flows instead of stopping at the first failed assertion. The two request-fixtured consumer flows and the homepage layout assertion passed; the search-input flow failed because the remote-denied local route never exposed the expected control. Three server/deployed-API declarations were excluded before execution. No source-bounded optimization candidate was produced.
products.memory_evidence: The peak includes runner and browser startup; it is not Anime renderer-heap attribution or leak evidence.
products.renderer_memory_evidence: A current recapture of the second flow retained 193 same-renderer Chromium counters over 839.141 ms. JS heap moved from 166792 to 22957152 bytes and peaked at 26583736 bytes; the final counter contained 673 DOM nodes, 4 documents, and 310 listeners. No leak is inferred without a repeated interaction and forced-GC comparison.
products.agent_facing_memory_evidence: The compact capture response for the first flow directly returned a process-tree peak of 879722496 bytes and 152 renderer samples with a 24965008-byte heap peak, while retaining leak_assessment as not_evaluated.
products.forced_gc_memory_evidence: The exact second flow completed three fresh-context repeats with forced GC before and after the unchanged test. Post-GC heap used was 20478276, 20550124, and 20578216 bytes (0.49% spread); all three samples retained 361 DOM nodes and 228 listeners. This is comparable local memory evidence, not same-page leak proof.
products.same_page_memory_evidence: The exact import-preview callback was captured twice with three same-page post-GC profiles per capture. One 66012-byte WatchlistView source appeared only in the first capture's third profile and disappeared on immediate repeat; same-page heap changed by -0.04% on the repeat, with DOM nodes fixed at 361 and listeners at 228. The product now requires a source in at least two profiles before promotion, so both artifacts normalize to no candidate. This is sampled-live accuracy evidence, not an optimization or leak verdict.
products.paired_browser_gate_evidence: Two self-contained clean worktrees at the identical revision completed a warm control and three alternating measured captures per side. Median root-flow time differed by +0.566%, renderer JavaScript by -0.043%, process-tree RSS by -0.548%, and final post-GC heap by -336 bytes; no repeated retention candidate appeared. The verifier correctly returned inconclusive. A second six-capture run stored browser-paired-7fd691a3f94d.json and terminated every owned runtime.
products.historical_candidate_evidence: A clean before/after replay evaluated Anime commit 4a16e16 under its statically declared mobile / iPhone 13 profile. Ten alternating pairs resolved a 390x664 viewport, scale 3, mobile emulation, and touch. Median LCP was 235.894 versus 237.337 ms (+0.612%), root-flow time regressed 0.399%, JavaScript regressed 2.325%, and process-tree RSS improved 0.602%; the verdict remained inconclusive. One candidate LCP sample was 26 ms while the other nine were near 237 ms, so the product now prevents unstable LCP distributions from confirming an optimization. A real autonomous mobile campaign also discarded the candidate at its three-pair screen. This remains local Chromium evidence, not production or field-device impact.
products.local_recommendation_optimization: A test-only contract used the real checked-in 14,841-title catalog with no database or network operation. CodeVetter independently selected scoreAnime in CPU and heap evidence. Computing rank scalars during the positive-limit scan and materializing full results only for bounded winners preserved an exact 12-case output hash. Three ten-sample runs improved full-catalog latency 38.284%-38.878%, conservative total application sampled allocation 60.2%-61.211%, and median process-tree RSS 5.824%-6.179%; all three were shipping-recommended. The full 137-test suite, typecheck, and lint pass.
products.react_redundancy_evidence: The public read-only operation selected four unused enum members and one internal-only constant export from the dirty revision-bound snapshot. Repository-wide reference and accessor review confirmed the boundary. Removing the four enum members and narrowing the constant export reduced the follow-up Knip inventory from five to zero; 137 tests, typecheck, lint, and the production build passed. This is static-hygiene evidence, not a performance or bundle-size claim. The declared jscpd payload was unavailable in the current local install, so implementation-clone coverage remains absent.
products.accuracy_improvement: Vite development resources, policy-denied requests, server-document assertions against a synthesized Vite origin, and one-profile sampled-live allocation noise can no longer become autonomous optimization work. A failed exact browser assertion is retained as flow evidence while later safe flows continue. Every exact Vitest pass now has fixed one-worker topology, and static JSON imports above 1 MiB receive a pre-execution harness-amplification safety flag.
products.next: Retain the homepage no-finding boundary and the local taste-recommendation win separately. Do not generalize the local catalog result to production frequency, D1 or network latency, browser responsiveness, or retained heap.

new_cross_project_proof.scope: performance-chart-model.test.ts / All has no lower bound
new_cross_project_proof.observed: The exact Jest adapter completed ten timing samples, two V8 profiles, and three separate memory passes. A later intent audit showed that investment performance in the filename is not software-performance evidence; autonomous selection now excludes it.

memory_policy.node: Three separate process-tree RSS passes provide a median regression guard. Two separate V8 sampling-allocation executions may retain up to eight material repository functions repeated in both, with CPU-aligned work first and secondary experiments constrained to the CPU candidate's file. In verification, the selected source activates a 20% plus 64 KiB exact-source gate and must agree with separated total application sampled-byte improvement; compatible RSS always retains its 10% plus 16 MiB regression gate. Sampled bytes are not exact retained bytes or leak evidence.
memory_policy.go: B/op, allocs/op, alloc_objects, and alloc_space evidence plus three separate process-tree RSS passes. Paired verification also alternates two pprof executions per side, normalizes direct alloc_objects by each run's benchmark iterations, and rejects an exact repeated source increase of at least 20% and 0.5 objects/op. Cumulative-only paths remain diagnostic. RSS directly executes a precompiled owned benchmark binary and excludes compilation and go test orchestration; it remains a regression guard rather than source attribution or independent proof of optimization.
memory_policy.browser: Exact owned Playwright flows retain one-run peak process-tree RSS, bounded same-renderer counters, and outer-main-frame LCP. Static named device or viewport projects become separate flow identities; receipts retain resolved viewport, scale, mobile, touch, and provenance without retaining the user agent. Request-fixtured flows additionally retain three fresh-context forced-GC samples plus three same-page post-GC sampled-live profiles. Paired React verification alternates at least three captures per side, requires byte-identical tests, the same resolved profile, and bounded sealed sources for every changed file, and gates stable root-flow timing, renderer phases, LCP, RSS, final post-GC heap, and repeated retention sources. This is local approximate evidence, not exact retained bytes, leak confirmation, representative-device behavior, or production impact.
memory_policy.verification: A change is rejected when peak RSS increases by at least 10% and 16 MiB on an otherwise compatible local scope.
